prompt: What does a hunt start from that an alert does not?

choices.text: A rule that the SIEM runs continuously against everything it receives
choices.why: That is alerting, the opposite direction.

choices.text: An indicator feed
choices.why: Feeds are looked up, not hunted.

choices.text: A ticket from a user
choices.why: That is a report, which may lead to triage.

choices.text: A hypothesis
choices.why: Right. An alert starts from a rule written in advance.

prompt: Why does the lesson reject browsing logs until something looks odd as a way of hunting?

choices.text: It is forbidden by the LGPD
choices.why: Reading your own security logs is not.

choices.text: Logs are too large to open
choices.why: Size is not the objection.

choices.text: Only the SIEM may read logs
choices.why: Analysts read logs all the time.

choices.text: It finds what is visually loud, and cannot be repeated or measured
choices.why: Right. A hunt needs a hypothesis, data, method and outcome that another analyst could rerun.

prompt: Match each hunt outcome to what happens next.

pairs.right: it is escalated to incident response
the question is never hunted by hand again

prompt: Which of these is a usable hunting hypothesis?

choices.text: The attackers are clever
choices.why: Not testable.

choices.text: We may have been hacked at some point
choices.why: No data, no test, nothing could prove it wrong.

choices.text: Check every log of the week for anything that looks strange or out of place
choices.why: That is browsing, not a hypothesis.

choices.text: If files was reached around gw, it logged another source
choices.why: Right. It names the data and the result that would refute it.

prompt: A hunting hypothesis has the shape: if this happened, ___ this would be in the data.
hint: The second half of a conditional.

prompt: Match each hypothesis to where it was inspired from.

pairs.left: H1, an account used from an address it never used
H2, files reached other than through gw
H3, logins at hours nobody works

choices.text: Rare things are always malicious
choices.why: A new employee is rare too.

choices.text: SQL sorts suspicious rows first
choices.why: It sorts by the count you ask for.

choices.text: Organisations repeat; attackers are rare
choices.why: Right. The rare end is where to look.

choices.text: Attackers always use the most common account names, which rise to the top of any count
choices.why: Bruno's rows were at the rare end, not the top of the count.

prompt: In H1's stack, how many successful logins did bruno's account make from 203.0.113.66?
Diego logs in to files from gw five times. Why is that not in the rare end with bruno's single hop?

choices.text: He uses a key, and key logins are excluded from the stack
choices.why: The stack counts every success.

choices.text: He is in IT, and IT accounts are never counted
choices.why: The stack counts every account.

choices.text: He does it every day, so it repeats like any habit
choices.why: Right. Repetition is what normal looks like.

choices.text: His logins happened at night
choices.why: They happen in the morning.

prompt: How many successful logins did H3's stack find between 02:00 and 03:59 local time?
What does validation use to confirm a rare row?

choices.text: Running the stacking query a second time to make sure the count is stable
choices.why: The same query gives the same answer; it confirms nothing new.

choices.text: Independent data the search did not use
choices.why: Right. For H1: the guessing before, the owner's normal login, the transfer after.

choices.text: A higher threshold
choices.why: Thresholds belong to rules.

choices.text: The analyst's intuition
choices.why: Validation is evidence, written down.

prompt: H2 came back negative. What makes that result worth relying on?

choices.text: The fact that six is a large number
choices.why: The size of the sample is not the point.

choices.text: It proves files is safe

choices.text: It was approved by a manager

prompt: What does the `backup` selection do in big-upload.yml?

choices.text: Drops the backup
choices.why: Right. Without it, every nightly backup would alert.

choices.text: Raises the rule's level at night
choices.why: There is no time condition.

choices.text: Selects only the backups
choices.why: It is negated in the condition.

choices.text: Copies the alert to the backup provider
choices.why: Selections choose events; they send nothing.

prompt: Which weakness of big-upload.yml does the lesson say belongs in its description?

choices.text: It says nothing about transfers under 100 MB
choices.why: Right. Splitting the upload stays under it.

choices.text: It alerts on every backup the company runs at night
choices.why: The backup is excluded.

choices.text: It cannot be converted to SQL by the SQLite backend of sigma-cli
choices.why: It converted and ran.

choices.text: It only works on Thursdays
choices.why: Nothing in it mentions a day.

choices.why: Tactics are fixed by the catalogue.
